name: Kaiming Liu
title: Physics PhD student
description: Kaiming Liu studies probabilistic machine learning, multimodal inference, and robustness in scientific inverse problems. Physics PhD student at UIUC.
bio: I study probabilistic machine learning, with a focus on multimodal inference and robustness under distribution shift.
I use scientific inverse problems to study multiple solutions and the shift from simulations to real measurements.
background: My experimental background informs how I approach the gap between simulations and measurements. In Vidya Madhavan’s group at UIUC, I grew thin films with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and studied electronic structure with STM/STS in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). I developed experimental automation and Python/MATLAB analysis of quasiparticle-interference data.
interests: Probabilistic machine learning; multimodal conditional inference; robustness under distribution shift; simulation-to-experiment transfer; neural many-body models.

education.degree: Special Class for the Gifted Young

experience.role: Graduate researcher, Bryan K. Clark group

projects.title: Multimodal inference / crystal-field parameters
bullets: Built residual-MLP conditional Gaussian mixtures to represent multiple plausible crystal-field solutions from susceptibility.
Validated candidates through forward reconstruction; studied noise, scale, and background shifts and experimental measurements.
Evaluated conditional Gaussian mixtures and conditional RealNVP normalizing flows in a pilot density-model comparison.

projects.title: Robust inverse prediction / neutron scattering
bullets: Trained MLP and ResNet conditional Gaussian mixtures for high-dimensional inverse prediction of exchange parameters from neutron maps.
Used exact Sunny forward evaluation and classical fit references; tested noise, intensity-scale, and background shifts.

projects.title: Neural-network backflow / JAX and Monte Carlo
bullets: Implemented neural-network backflow and variational Monte Carlo in JAX for Hubbard models, with GPU/multi-GPU sampling.
Profiled local-energy evaluation and gradient synchronization; verified chunked evaluation and global reductions against reference computations.
Grew thin-film heterostructures with MBE and characterized electronic structure with STM/STS in ultrahigh vacuum.
Automated growth temperature control and built Python/MATLAB tools for quasiparticle-interference analysis.
Simulated Rydberg-atom dynamics and photon-mediated interactions in Python/MATLAB to study quantum nonlinear optics.
Built a discrete-time lattice model of two-qubit phase-flip dynamics and many-body regimes.

experience.role: Research assistant, Michael F. Crommie group
bullets: Assisted synthesis and STM characterization of graphene nanoribbons with five-membered rings to study their electronic states.

teaching.text: Led discussion and laboratory sections, held office hours, and provided feedback on assignments in electromagnetism and modern physics.
